paragraphs: Monocle Acquisition Corporation ("Monocle") was initially formed as a Delaware corporation on August 20, 2018 for the purpose of effecting a merger, share exchange, asset acquisition, stock purchase, recapitalization, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses.

On December 22, 2020, Monocle consummated the previously announced business combination pursuant to that certain Amended and Restated Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated September 8, 2020 (the "Merger Agreement") by and among Monocle, the Company, AerSale Aviation, Inc. (f/k/a AerSale Corp.), a Delaware corporation ("AerSale Aviation"), Monocle Merger Sub 1 Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Merger Sub 1"), Monocle Merger Sub 2 LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Merger Sub 2"), and Leonard Green & Partners, L.P., a Delaware limited partnership, solely in its capacity as the initial Holder Representative (as defined in the Merger Agreement). The transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement are referred to herein as the "Merger" or the "Business Combination" and in connection therewith, Monocle merged with and into us, whereby we survived the merger and became the successor issuer to Monocle by operation of Rule 12g-3 under the Exchange Act.

Upon the consummation of the Merger: (a) Merger Sub 1 was merged with and into Monocle, with Monocle surviving the merger as a wholly-owned direct subsidiary of the Company, and (b) Merger Sub 2 was merged with and into AerSale Aviation, with AerSale Aviation surviving the merger as a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of the Company. In connection with the closing of the Business Combination, AerSale Aviation changed its name from "AerSale Corp." to "AerSale Aviation, Inc." and the Company changed its name from "Monocle Holdings Inc." to "AerSale Corporation." Immediately following the Merger, the Company contributed all of its ownership in Monocle to AerSale Aviation, which continued as a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

Our mission is to provide full-service support to owners and operators of mid-life commercial aircraft who lack the infrastructure and/or expertise to cost-effectively maintain such aircraft during the second half of their operating life through their retirement from service. By providing a one-stop shop that integrates multiple service and product offerings, we save our customers time and money, while providing value to our stockholders through our operating efficiency. We were founded in 2008 by Nicolas Finazzo and Robert B. Nichols as a platform to serve the aviation aftermarket. In early 2010, we partnered with private equity firm Leonard Green & Partners, L.P. to scale our business and finance the creation of a purpose built and fully integrated aviation company. Since our founding, we have established a global footprint and scalable platform for growth.

Our business is comprised of two reporting segments: Asset Management Solutions and Technical Operations ("TechOps"), which, taken together, provide comprehensive support to owners and operators of used commercial aircraft.

Our Asset Management Solutions segment, which represented approximately 63% and 62% of our revenue during the fiscal years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, acquires Flight Equipment from airlines and leasing companies as feedstock to support our business activities. Asset Management Solutions activities include the sale and lease of aircraft and engines, as well as the disassembly of these assets for component parts (such as used serviceable material ("USM")) that can be utilized to support third-party sales and lower the cost to maintain our portfolio of leased assets. Our aircraft and engines generally provide highly customized full-service, short-term lease support, where an operator is provided with a turn-key piece of Flight Equipment that can meet the customer's specific needs. Our business model provides an alternative to the procurement of new aircraft, engines and parts traditionally sold by original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs") or delivered new and leased by pure-play aircraft and engine leasing companies. Because we have created the infrastructure to market through alternative channels, we are able to maximize financial returns on Flight Equipment by cost-effectively placing such assets in the secondary market for the balance of their operating life, and upon retirement from service, extracting their greatest residual value by disassembling Flight Equipment assets to the piece-part level for re-use as USM. We do this by utilizing our integrated business units to maximize the sum of each asset's alternative revenue streams, ranging from their sale or lease as whole operating assets, down to utilizing their collective individual components to serve as USM feedstock or to lower our leasing and operating costs related to MRO services. We also offer our integrated Asset Management Solutions services to third-party clients who lack the expertise and/or infrastructure to optimize their Flight Equipment investments. We lease engines and airframes primarily as a means of extracting value from the remaining operating life of an asset prior to disassembly for USM parts. We focus primarily on highly customized aircraft leases or short-term engine leasing where we can demand a lease premium, and we utilize our USM and MRO capabilities to fully meet all maintenance needs, which allow us to fully monetize collected maintenance reserves. After disassembly, we utilize the components as low-cost spare parts feedstock to support our various other business segments, including USM part sales, and in conjunction with our third-party maintenance operations. Consequently, the vast majority of aircraft and engines that we have acquired have ultimately been disassembled for their USM parts once the full value of their remaining operating life has been extracted.

Our TechOps segment, which represented approximately 37% and 38% of our revenue during the fiscal years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, provides nose-to-tail MRO services on the most popular commercial aircraft, engines, and components that serve the passenger, cargo, and government sectors. Through our collective U.S.-based MRO facilities, we provide extensive maintenance and modification services for aircraft and their individual components. Our aircraft facilities located in Goodyear, Arizona, Roswell, New Mexico, and Millington, Tennessee collectively feature approximately 530,000 square feet of hangar space, from which we provide high-quality airframe MRO services, structural modification, conversions, and flight system upgrades, including disassembly and re-cycling operations for retiring aircraft. We additionally offer convenient long-term storage capacity for up to 650 aircraft in ideal dry-desert conditions.

At the individual component level, our facilities located in Miami, Florida, Hialeah Gardens, Florida, Rio Rancho, New Mexico, and Millington, Tennessee collectively offer specialized component MRO capabilities and services covering

hydraulics, composites, pneumatics, fuel systems, electro-mechanical assemblies, interiors, painting, flight controls, nacelles, and landing gear for passenger, cargo, and military aircraft applications.

Our TechOps segment leverages its robust engineering team to provide highly specialized technical support to our MRO facilities, as well as to develop advanced technical repairs, modifications and products, which we market under the tradename "Engineered Solutions." This business unit includes the design, manufacture, and installation of new products, systems, and services that can enhance aircraft performance, safety, and service life at lower costs than traditionally expensive OEM products and services. Engineered Solutions also serves to lower the cost of Flight Equipment ownership with savings on MRO-related expenses, including compliance with mandatory and market-driven equipment upgrades. These cost-saving solutions are approved by the Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA") under Supplemental Type Certificates ("STCs"), which provide us with the unique ability to perform these modifications. We use our FAA-approved Parts Manufacturing Authority ("PMA") to integrate third party components in developing our STC solutions. We have also obtained approval from various foreign regulatory authorities to validate our STCs and PMA products for use by operators outside of the United States.

Examples of our Engineered Solutions products are AerSafe® and AerAware® product lines. We designed and received FAA approval to market AerSafe® as a solution for compliance with an FAA mandate to mitigate aircraft fuel tank flammability on Boeing and Airbus aircraft. AerSafe® has also been approved for installation on certain aircraft models that are regulated by the European Aviation Safety Agency ("EASA") and the National Civil Aviation Agency of Brazil. Another example of our Engineered Solutions is our AerAware™ product, an industry-leading, next generation Enhanced Flight Vision System ("EFVS") that provides pilots with unparalleled visibility through the use of synthetic and enhanced vision, allowing pilots a greater level of visibility and control while operating the aircraft. This product has received approval by the FAA for the Boeing B737NG product line.

The aviation aftermarket is highly competitive with many participants, including Flight Equipment OEMs, MRO providers, airlines, aircraft and engine leasing companies, financial sponsors, USM sales organizations, and other independent manufacturers and service providers. The vast majority of participants compete within smaller subsets of our broader products and services offerings. Frequently, our competitors specialize in one or a limited number of areas within the following segments: aircraft MRO, engine MRO, Engineered Solutions, aircraft leasing, engine leasing, USM part sales, and asset management. Further, many component MRO providers specialize in a small subset of repairs related to specific components or materials, such as composites, pneumatics, hydraulics, electronics, landing gear, wheels and brakes, and auxiliary power units.

Consumers of aftermarket Flight Equipment products and services typically make buying decisions based on a variety of factors including quality, pricing, availability, provider reputation, technical specification, prior operating history, turnaround time, geographic location and financial terms.

Our Asset Management Solutions segment competitors include AAR Corp., AerCap, Delta Air Lines, Inc., GA Telesis, LLC, Kellstrom Aerospace, Heico Corporation, Willis Lease Finance Corp, Air Transport Services Group, LLC, Unical Aviation, Inc, Satair Group, Aviall, Inc, and FTAI Aviation, while competitors to our TechOps segment include AAR Corp., Aviation Technical Services, Inc., HAECO Americas, MRO Holdings, Inc., ST Engineering North America, Air Transport Services Group, LLC, Delta TechOps, TransDigm Group, VSE Corporation, Woodward, Inc., Lufthansa Technik AG, and Triumph Group. Though our product and service offerings include certain aircraft and engine leasing activities, we do not view large pure-play aircraft and engine leasing companies as core competitors, as those companies are primarily centered around cost of capital and financial securitization products, and frequently choose to divest mid-life assets as they lack the technical and mechanical capabilities to deal with assets that have exited the OEM warranty periods.

headings: Risks Related to AerSale's Business and Industry
Supply chain disruptions could have adverse effects on our ability to provide certain services.
We are affected by factors that adversely impact the commercial aviation industry.
Market values for our aviation products fluctuate, and we may be unable to recover our costs incurred with respect to engines, rotable components and other aircraft parts.
Success at our MRO facilities is dependent upon continued outsourcing by the airlines.
Our operations would be adversely affected by a shortage of skilled personnel or work stoppages.
The inability to obtain certain components and raw materials from suppliers could harm our business.
We operate in highly competitive markets, and competitive pressures may adversely affect us.
We are exposed to risks associated with operating internationally.
Business acquisitions expose us to risks, including the risk that we may be unable to effectively integrate acquired businesses.
Further consolidation in the aerospace industry could adversely affect our business and financial results.
Our business could be negatively affected by cyber or other security threats or other disruptions.
We may need to make significant capital expenditures to keep pace with technological developments in our industry.
We do not own certain intellectual property and tooling that is important to our business.
We could become involved in intellectual property litigation, which could have a material and adverse impact on our profitability.
Our operations depend on our facilities, which are subject to physical and other risks that could disrupt production.
Our business might suffer if we were to lose the services of certain key employees.
If our subcontractors or suppliers fail to perform their contractual obligations, our contract profitability and our ability to win new contracts may be adversely affected.
Future outbreaks and infectious diseases could have a material adverse impact on our business, operating results, financial condition, and liquidity.
Strategic and Financial Risks
We are dependent upon continued availability of financing to manage our business and to execute our business strategy, and additional financing may not be available on terms acceptable to us.
Our existing debt includes restrictive and financial covenants.
Unanticipated changes in our tax provision or exposure to additional income tax liabilities could affect our profitability.
Our financial results of operations could be adversely affected by impairment of our goodwill or other intangible assets.
Our exposure to variable interest rates and foreign currency exchange rates could materially and adversely affect our business, operating results and financial condition.
Legal and Regulatory Risks
We are subject to significant government regulation and may need to incur significant expenses to comply with new or more stringent governmental regulation.
We are subject to the FCPA and other anti-corruption laws, as well as export control laws, import and customs laws, trade and economic sanctions laws and other laws governing our operations.
Our business and financial results may be affected by various litigation and regulatory proceedings.
Liens on our Flight Equipment could exceed the value of such Flight Equipment, which could negatively affect our ability to repossess, lease or sell such Flight Equipment.
In certain countries, an engine affixed to an aircraft may become an accession to the aircraft and we may not be able to exercise our ownership rights over the engine.
Our industry is susceptible to product and other liability claims, and claims not adequately covered by insurance may adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
We must comply with extensive environmental requirements, and any exposure to environmental liabilities may adversely affect us.
We may be adversely affected by global climate change, or by legal, regulatory or market responses to such change.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below and the other information in this Annual Report before making an investment in our common stock. Our business, financial condition, results of operations, or prospects could be materially and adversely affected if any of these risks occurs, and as a result, the market price of our common stock could decline and you could lose all or part of your investment. This Annual Report also contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. See "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" in this Annual Report. Our actual results could differ materially and adversely from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of certain factors, including those set forth below.

We source parts and components for our business from various suppliers around the world. Current geopolitical conditions, including sanctions and other trade restrictive actions and intercountry relations, could cause significant materials and parts shortages, as well as delivery delays, labor shortages, distribution issues, energy cost increases and price increases. These issues could lead to significant supplier performance failures and delays. Disruptions to our supply chain and business operations, or to our suppliers' supply chains and business operations, could have adverse effects on our ability to provide aftermarket support and services to our customers.

As a provider of products and services to the commercial aviation industry, we are generally affected by overall economic conditions of that industry. The commercial aviation industry is historically cyclical and has been negatively affected in the past by geopolitical events, such as political instability (including between Russia and Ukraine, between Israel and Hamas, and most recently, as a result of military action in Iran by the U.S. and Israel), escalating tensions (such as between China and the U.S.), terrorism, high fuel and oil prices, labor issues, lack of capital, continued inflation, high interest rates, and weak economic conditions. As a result of these and other events, from time to time certain of our customers have filed for bankruptcy protection or ceased operations. The impact of instability in the global financial markets has led, and may in the future lead, airlines to reduce domestic or international capacity. In addition, certain of our airline customers have in the past been impacted by tight credit markets, which limited their ability to buy parts, services, and Flight Equipment.

A reduction in flight activity of aircraft both in the United States and abroad has resulted in, and may continue to result in, reduced demand for parts support and maintenance activities for the type of aircraft affected. Further, tight credit conditions negatively impact the amount of liquidity available to buy parts, services, and Flight Equipment. A deteriorating airline environment may also result in additional airline bankruptcies, and in such circumstances, we may not be able to fully collect outstanding accounts receivable. Reduced demand from customers caused by weak economic conditions, including tight credit conditions and customer bankruptcies, may adversely impact our financial condition or results of operations. A slowdown in the global economy, or a recession, would negatively impact the commercial aviation industry, and may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, liquidity and results of operations.

Our ability to profitably manage mid-life Flight Equipment through the end of its life-cycles depends in part on our ability to successfully source acquisition opportunities of used Flight Equipment on favorable terms to provide feedstock for the sale of USM parts. Our inability to acquire Flight Equipment could adversely affect our financial condition or results of operations. Our business, financial condition, results of operations, and growth rates may be

paragraphs: You should read the following management's discussion and analysis together with the Consolidated Financial Statements. This discussion contains forward-looking statements about AerSale's business, operations and industry that involve risks and uncertainties, such as statements regarding AerSale's plans, objectives, expectations and intentions. AerSale's future results and financial condition may differ materially from those currently anticipated by AerSale because of the factors described in the sections entitled "Risk Factors" and "Special Note Regarding Forward-looking Statements." A discussion of the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the year ended December 31, 2023 is included in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, filed with the SEC on March 11, 2025, under Part II, Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations."

We operate as a platform for serving the commercial aviation aftermarket sector. Our top executives have on average over 30 years of experience in aircraft and engine ("Flight Equipment") management, sales and maintenance services, and are supported by an experienced management team. We have established a global purpose built and fully integrated aviation company focused on providing products and services that maximize the value of Flight Equipment in the middle to end of its operating life cycle.

We are a worldwide provider of aftermarket commercial aircraft, engines, and their parts to passenger and cargo airlines, leasing companies, original equipment manufacturers ("OEM"), government and defense contractors, and maintenance, repair and overhaul ("MRO") service providers. We report our activities in two business segments: Asset Management Solutions, comprised of activities that extract value from strategic Flight Equipment acquisitions either as whole assets or by disassembling for used serviceable material ("USM"), and TechOps, comprised of MRO activities for aircraft and their components, sales of internally developed advanced technical repairs, modifications and products, which we market under the tradename "Engineered Solutions", and other serviceable products.

Our Asset Management Solutions segment focuses on mid-life Flight Equipment. Asset Management Solutions' activities include monetization of assets through the lease or sale of whole assets, or through disassembly activities in support of our USM-related activities. Our monetizing services have been developed to maximize returns on mid-life Flight Equipment throughout their operating life, in conjunction with realizing the highest residual value of Flight Equipment at its retirement. We accomplish this by utilizing deep market and technical knowledge related to the management of Flight Equipment sales, leasing and MRO services. To extract value from the remaining flight time on whole assets, we provide flexible short-term (generally less than five years) leasing solutions of Flight Equipment to passenger and cargo operators across the globe. Once the value from the Flight Equipment's flight time has been extracted, Flight Equipment is considered to be at or near the end of its useful life and is analyzed for return maximization as either whole asset sales or disassembled for sale as USM parts. Revenue from this segment is segregated between Aircraft and Engine depending on the asset type that generated the revenue. Lease revenue and the related depreciation from aircraft and engines installed on those aircraft are recognized under the Aircraft category. Revenue from sales of whole aircraft and related cost of sales are allocated between the Aircraft and Engine categories based on the allocated cost basis of the asset sold.

Our TechOps segment provides internal and third-party aviation services, including internally developed Engineered Solutions, full heavy aircraft maintenance and modification, component MRO, as well as end-of-life disassembly services to all Flight Equipment. Our MRO business also engages in longer-term projects such as aircraft modifications, cargo and tanker conversions of aircraft, and aircraft storage. The TechOps segment also includes MRO services for landing gear, thrust reversers, hydraulic systems, and other aircraft components.

We utilize these capabilities to support our customers' Flight Equipment, as well as to maintain and improve our own Flight Equipment, which is subsequently sold or leased to our customers. These processes require a high degree of expertise on each individual aircraft or component that is being serviced. Our knowledge of these processes allows us to assist customers to comply with applicable regulatory and OEM requirements. A significant amount of skilled labor is required to support this process, which the Company has accumulated through its diversified offerings.

In addition to our aircraft and USM parts offerings, we develop Engineered Solutions consisting of Supplemental Type Certificates ("STCs") that can be installed on existing Flight Equipment to improve performance, comply with regulatory requirements, or improve safety. An example of these solutions is the AerSafe® product line, which we designed and for which we obtained Federal Aviation Administration (the "FAA") approval to sell as a solution for compliance with the FAA's fuel tank flammability regulations. Another example of these solutions is our AerAware™ product, an industry-leading, next generation Enhanced Flight Vision System that has recently received approval by the FAA for the Boeing B737NG product line. These products are proprietary in nature and function as non-OEM solutions to regulatory requirements and other technical challenges, often at reduced delivery time and cost for operators. In order to develop these products, we engage in research and development ("R&D") activities that are expensed as incurred.

We source parts and components for our business from various suppliers around the world. Current geopolitical conditions, including trade restrictive actions, strained intercountry relations, and continued shutdowns of the U.S. government, could cause significant materials and parts shortages, as well as delivery delays, labor shortages, disruptions to government contracts such as delayed payments or halted projects, effects on supply chains due to reduced staffing for customs, inspections and transportation authorities, or delays in regulatory approvals, distribution issues, energy cost increases and price increases. Furthermore, the U.S. government's adoption of new approaches to trade policy and imposition of tariffs on certain foreign goods (as well as the possibility of imposing significant, additional tariffs in the future) may make it more difficult or costly for us to procure components and other material supplies and, in turn, may increase the cost to our customers, which may materially and adversely impact demand for our products and services, our results of operations or our financial condition. In addition, these U.S. actions have, and could in the future, result in other countries imposing retaliatory tariffs on our goods and services provided to foreign customers, which similarly could materially and adversely impact demand for our products and services. We continue to monitor the current economic environment and its potential impact on our business, results of operations or financial condition, as well as potential impact on our end customers whose demand for our products and services may be adversely impacted as a result of changes in policies by the U.S. or other governments, and closely manage our costs and capital resources so that we can respond appropriately as circumstances change.

paragraphs: Monocle Acquisition Corporation ("Monocle") 於 2018 年 8 月 20 日在特拉華州成立為一家公司，其目的為進行合併、股權交換、資產收購、股票購買、資本重組或類似商業結合，與一家或多間企業。

Monocle 於 2020 年 12 月 22 日完成先前宣佈的商業結合，根據 2020 年 9 月 8 日簽訂的修正並重述之合併協議與合併計劃 ("Merger Agreement")，由 Monocle、本公司、AerSale Aviation, Inc. (f/k/a AerSale Corp.)，一家特拉華州公司 ("AerSale Aviation")、Monocle Merger Sub 1 Inc.，一家特拉華州公司 ("Merger Sub 1")、Monocle Merger Sub 2 LLC，一家特拉華州有限責任公司 ("Merger Sub 2")，以及 Leonard Green & Partners, L.P.，一家特拉華州有限合作夥伴，僅以其作為初始持有人代表 (如 Merger Agreement 所定義) 之資格。根據 Merger Agreement 所預期的交易， herein 稱為 "Merger" 或 "Business Combination"，並於此連帶，Monocle 與我們合併，我們存活於合併後成為 Monocle 的繼承發行者，根據證券交易法 (Exchange Act) 之 Rule 12g-3。

在完成 Merger 後：(a) Merger Sub 1 與 Monocle 合併，Monocle 存活於合併後成為本公司之 wholly-owned 直屬子公司，以及 (b) Merger Sub 2 與 AerSale Aviation 合併，AerSale Aviation 存活於合併後成為本公司之 wholly-owned 間接子公司。在 Business Combination 交易完成時，AerSale Aviation 將其名稱從 "AerSale Corp." 改為 "AerSale Aviation, Inc."，本公司將其名稱從 "Monocle Holdings Inc." 改為 "AerSale Corporation." 在 Merger 完成後，本公司將其對 Monocle 的全部股權轉讓給 AerSale Aviation，AerSale Aviation 繼續作為本公司之 wholly owned 子公司。

我們的使命是為缺乏基礎設施和/或專業知識，以成本效益方式維護其飛機至其使用壽命後半段並在退役前的中年商用飛機所有者和運營者提供全服務支援。透過提供整合多種服務與產品的單一服務點，我們為客戶節省時間與金錢，同時透過我們的運營效率為股東創造價值。我們於 2008 年由 Nicolas Finazzo 和 Robert B. Nichols 聯手創立，作為服務航空後市場的平台。在 2010 年初，我們與私人股權公司 Leonard Green & Partners, L.P. 合作，以擴大我們的業務並為建立一家專門且完全整合的航空公司提供資金。自我們成立以來，我們已建立全球足跡與可擴展的成長平台。
我們的業務包含兩個應報告分部：資產管理解決方案與技術運營 ("TechOps")，這兩個分部共同為使用過的商用飛機所有者和運營者提供全面支援。

我們的資產管理解決方案分部，於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務年度及 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度，分別約佔我們營業收入的 63% 和 62%，從航空公司及租賃公司取得飛機與引擎作為原料，以支持我們的業務活動。資產管理解決方案活動包括飛機與引擎的銷售與租賃，以及拆解這些資產以取得零組件 (如已使用可維修材料 ("USM"))，這些零組件可用於支援第三方銷售並降低我們租賃資產組合的維護成本。我們的飛機與引擎通常提供高度客製化的短暫租賃支援，運營者可獲得一整套飛機設備，以符合客戶的特定需求。我們的業務模式提供一種替代傳統原廠設備製造商 ("OEMs") 或由純粹航空與引擎租賃公司銷售新機與引擎的選擇。因為我們已建立透過替代通路進行行銷的基礎設施，我們能透過成本效益方式將飛機設備置於次級市場，以充分利用其使用壽命，並在飛機退役時，透過拆解飛機設備至零組件層面以提取其最大殘值。我們透過整合的業務單位來最大化每個資產的替代收入流，從其作為整體運營資產的銷售或租賃，一直到利用其個別零組件作為 USM 原料或降低我們與 MRO 服務相關的租賃與運營成本。我們也為缺乏專業知識與/或基礎設施的第三方客戶提供我們整合的資產管理解決方案服務。我們主要租賃引擎與機身，作為從資產的剩餘使用壽命中提取價值的手段，再拆解為 USM 零組件。我們主要聚焦於高度客製化的飛機租賃或短期引擎租賃，我們能要求租賃 premium，並利用我們的 USM 與 MRO 能力完全滿足所有維護需求，這使我們能完全實現所收集的維護儲備。拆解後，我們利用這些零組件作為低成本備件原料，以支援我們的其他業務部門，包括 USM 零組件銷售，並與我們的第三方維護運營結合。因此，我們所取得的飛機與引擎，最終大多數都已拆解為 USM 零組件，以提取其剩餘使用壽命的全部價值。

我們的 TechOps 分部，於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務年度及 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度，分別約佔我們營業收入的 37% 和 38%，為最流行的商用飛機、引擎與零組件提供從機頭到機尾的 MRO 服務，這些飛機、引擎與零組件服務於乘客、貨運與政府部門。透過我們位於美國的 MRO 基礎設施，我們為飛機及其個別零組件提供廣泛的維護與修改服務。我們位於 Goodyear, Arizona、Roswell, New Mexico 與 Millington, Tennessee 的飛機設施，總計擁有約 530,000 平方英尺的機庫空間，我們從此提供高品質的機身 MRO 服務、結構修改、轉換與飛行系統升級，包括拆解與再循環操作，以處理退役飛機。我們也提供方便的長期儲存空間，最多可儲存 650 架飛機，於理想乾燥沙漠條件下。
在個別零組件層面，我們位於 Miami, Florida、Hialeah Gardens, Florida、Rio Rancho, New Mexico 與 Millington, Tennessee 的設施，總計提供專門的零組件 MRO 能力與服務，涵蓋
液壓系統、複合材料、氣壓系統、燃料系統、電機機械組裝、內裝、塗裝、飛行控制、引擎罩、及起落架，用於客機、貨機及軍用飛機應用。

我們的 TechOps 分部利用其強大的工程團隊，為我們的 MRO 基設提供高度專業化的技術支援，並開發先進的技術維修、改裝與產品，這些產品我們以 tradename "Engineered Solutions" 進行市場推廣。此業務單位包括設計、製造與安裝新產品、系統與服務，這些產品、系統與服務可以較傳統昂貴的 OEM 產品與服務更低的成本，提升飛機性能、安全性與使用壽命。Engineered Solutions 也用以降低飛機設備擁有成本，透過節省 MRO 相關費用，包括符合強制性與市場驅動的設備升級。這些節省成本的解決方案已獲得美國聯邦航空管理局（"FAA"）在補充型飛機認證（"STCs"）下的批准，這使我們擁有獨特的能力執行這些改裝。我們使用 FAA 批准的零件製造權（"PMA"）來整合第三方零組件，以開發我們的 STC 解決方案。我們也已獲得多個外國監管機構的批准，以驗證我們的 STCs 與 PMA 產品，供於美國以外的運營者使用。

我們的 Engineered Solutions 產品範例包括 AerSafe® 與 AerAware® 產品線。我們設計並獲得 FAA 批准，將 AerSafe® 作為符合 FAA 命令的解決方案，用以降低飛機燃料箱易燃性問題，適用於波音與空中巴士飛機。AerSafe® 也已獲得安裝於某些由歐洲航空安全局（"EASA"）與巴西國家民用航空局所規範的飛機模型的批准。另一個我們 Engineered Solutions 的範例是我們的 AerAware™ 產品，這是一款行業領先的下一代增強飛行視野系統（"EFVS"），透過合成與增強視野的使用，為飛行員提供無與倫比的視野，使飛行員在操作飛機時擁有更高的視野與控制能力。此產品已獲得 FAA 對波音 B737NG 產品線的批准。

航空後市場高度競爭，參與者眾多，包括飛機設備 OEM、MRO 提供商、航空公司、飛機與發動機租賃公司、財務投資者、USM 壽命銷售組織，以及其他獨立製造商與服務提供者。絕大多數參與者競爭的範圍，僅限於我們較廣泛產品與服務中的較小子集。經常，我們的競爭對手專注於以下段落中的一個或幾個有限領域：飛機 MRO、發動機 MRO、Engineered Solutions、飛機租賃、發動機租賃、USM 零組件銷售與資產管理。此外，許多零組件 MRO 提供商專注於與特定零組件或材料相關的有限修理，例如複合材料、氣壓系統、液壓系統、電子產品、起落架、輪胎與剎車，以及輔助動力單元。
後市場飛機設備產品與服務的消費者通常根據多種因素做出購買決定，包括品質、價格、可取得性、提供者聲譽、技術規格、過去運作紀錄、處理時間、地理位置與財務條件。

我們的資產管理解決方案分部競爭對手包括 AAR Corp.、AerCap、Delta Air Lines, Inc.、GA Telesis, LLC、Kellstrom Aerospace、Heico Corporation、Willis Lease Finance Corp、Air Transport Services Group, LLC、Unical Aviation, Inc、Satair Group、Aviall, Inc、FTAi Aviation，而我們的 TechOps 分部競爭對手則包括 AAR Corp.、Aviation Technical Services, Inc.、HAECO Americas、MRO Holdings, Inc.、ST Engineering North America、Air Transport Services Group, LLC、Delta TechOps、TransDigm Group、VSE Corporation、Woodward, Inc.、Lufthansa Technik AG、以及 Triumph Group。儘管我們的產品與服務包含某些飛機與發動機租賃活動，我們並不將大型純粹飛機與發動機租賃公司視為核心競爭對手，因為這些公司主要聚焦於資金成本與財務證券化產品，且經常選擇出售中年資產，因為他們缺乏處理已離開 OEM 保固期的資產的技術與機械能力。

paragraphs: 您應配合審閱財務報表，一併閱讀下列管理層討論與分析。此討論包含有關 AerSale 事業、營運與產業的展望性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性，例如有關 AerSale 計畫、目標、預期與意圖的陳述。AerSale 未來的結果與財務狀況可能與目前預期的有重大差異，原因在於所描述的風險因素及「展望性陳述特別說明」部分。有關 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年與 2023 年 12 月 31 日財年比較的討論，請參閱我們 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年 10-K 年度報告，於 2025 年 3 月 11 日提交至 SEC，位於第二部分，第 7 項「財務狀況與營運結果之管理層討論與分析」。
我們營運為服務商業航空後市場產業的平台。我們的高階主管平均擁有超過 30 年的飛機與引擎（「飛行設備」）管理、銷售與維修服務經驗，並由經驗豐富的管理團隊支援。我們已建立一家全球性專門打造且完全整合的航空公司，專注於提供產品與服務，以最大化飛行設備在其運作壽命中段至末段的價值。

我們是全球後市場商業飛機、引擎及其零組件的供應商，服務於乘客與貨運航空公司、租賃公司、原廠設備製造商（「OEM」）、政府與防衛承包商，以及維修、保養與翻修（「MRO」）服務供應商。我們將業務活動分為兩個應報告分部：資產管理解決方案，包含從戰略飛行設備採購中提取價值的活動，無論是整體資產或拆解以取得可用服務零組件（「USM」）；以及 TechOps，包含飛機及其零組件的 MRO 活動、銷售 internally developed 高階技術修理、修改與產品，我們以 tradename「Engineered Solutions」行銷，以及其他可用服務零組件。

我們的資產管理解決方案分部專注於中段飛行設備。資產管理解決方案的活動包括透過出租或出售整體資產，或透過拆解活動支持我們的 USM 相關活動，來實現資產的價值。我們的 monetizing 服務已發展以最大化中段飛行設備在其運作壽命中的回報，並在飛行設備退休時實現最高的殘值。我們透過對飛行設備銷售、出租及 MRO 服務的市場與技術知識來達成此目標。為從整體資產的飛行時間中提取價值，我們提供全球範圍內的靈活短期（通常少於五年）出租解決方案給乘客與貨運運營商。一旦從飛行設備的飛行時間中提取價值，飛行設備就被認為處於或接近其使用壽命末段，並分析作為整體資產銷售或拆解以銷售為 USM 零組件，以實現價值最大化。此分部的收入根據產生收入的資產類型，分為飛機與引擎。出租收入及相關折舊費用，根據安裝在飛機上的飛機與引擎，歸入飛機類別。銷售整體飛機及相關銷售成本，根據出售資產的分配成本基礎，分為飛機與引擎類別。

我們的 TechOps 分部提供內部與第三方航空服務，包括 internally developed Engineered Solutions、完整的重型飛機維修與修改、零組件 MRO，以及所有飛行設備的終期拆解服務。我們的 MRO 事業也參與較長的專案，例如飛機修改、貨運與油罐機的飛機轉換，以及飛機儲存。TechOps 分部也包括著陸 gear、推力反轉器、液壓系統及其他飛機零組件的 MRO 服務。
我們利用這些能力來支援我們客戶的飛行設備，同時也用來維護與改善我們自己的飛行設備，這些飛行設備隨後會出售或出租給我們的客戶。這些過程需要對每一架飛機或零組件進行高度專業的技術知識。我們對這些過程的瞭解，使我們能協助客戶符合適用的法規與 OEM 要求。這些過程需要大量專業人力，本公司已透過多元化的產品與服務累積了這些人力。

除了我們的飛機與 USM 零組件產品，我們開發 Engineered Solutions，包含可安裝在現有飛行設備上的補充類型證書（「STC」），以改善性能、符合法規要求或提高安全性。這些解決方案的範例包括 AerSafe® 產品線，我們設計並取得美國聯邦航空管理局（「FAA」）批准，作為符合 FAA 燃油箱易燃性法規的解決方案。另一個範例是我們的 AerAware™ 產品，這是一款行業領先的下一代增強飛行視覺系統，最近已獲得 FAA 對 Boeing B737NG 產品線的批准。這些產品具有專利性質，作為非 OEM 解決方案，用以符合法規要求及其他技術挑戰，通常能以較低的交付時間與成本提供給運營商。為開發這些產品，我們進行研究與發展（「R&D」）活動，並於發生時費用化。

我們從世界各地的供應商處取得我們業務所需的零件與零組件。目前的國際政治環境，包括貿易限制措施、國家間關係緊張，以及美國政府持續關閉，可能會導致重大材料與零件短缺，以及交付延誤、勞工短缺、政府合同的中斷，例如付款延遲或專案中止，因減少的關稅、檢查與運輸機構人力而導致供應鏈受影響，或延遲法規批准、分銷問題、能源成本增加與價格上漲。此外，美國政府採用新的貿易政策方法並對某些外國商品徵收關稅（以及未來可能徵收重大額外關稅的可能），可能使我們更難或更貴地取得零件與其他材料供應，進而增加我們客戶的成本，這可能會對我們產品與服務的需求、營運結果或財務狀況造成重大且不利的影響。此外，這些美國行動已導致，且未來可能導致其他國家對我們提供給外國客戶的產品與服務徵收報復性關稅，這也會對我們產品與服務的需求造成重大且不利的影響。我們持續監測目前的經濟環境及其對我們業務、營運結果或財務狀況的潛在影響，以及對我們終端客戶的潛在影響，這些客戶對我們產品與服務的需求可能因美國或其他政府的政策變動而受到不利影響，我們也密切管理我們的成本與資本資源，以便在情況變化時做出適當回應。
AerSale 兩個業務應報告分部於 2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度及 2024 年 12 月 31 日會計年度之銷售及毛利如下：
2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度總營業收入較 2024 年減少 9.8 百萬美元或 2.8%，主因為資產管理解決方案減少 3.9 百萬美元，或 1.8%，以及 TechOps 減少 5.9 百萬美元，或 4.5%。

headings: 與 AerSale 事業與產業相關之風險
供應鏈中斷可能對我們提供特定服務之能力產生不利影響。
我們受影響於對商業航空產業產生不利影響之因素。
我們航空產品之市場價值波動，我們可能無法回收針對引擎、可更換零組件及其他飛機零件所產生之成本。
我們 MRO 設施之成功取決於航空公司持續委外合作。
我們之營運若因缺乏具備技能之人力或罷工而受影響，將產生不利影響。
無法從供應商取得特定零組件及原材料可能損害我們之業務。
我們營運於高度競爭之市場，競爭壓力可能對我們產生不利影響。
本公司面臨與國際營運相關之風險。
企業併購使本公司面臨風險，包括無法有效整合所收購之企業之風險。
航空產業進一步集中可能對本公司業務及財務結果產生不利影響。
本公司業務可能因網路或其它安全威脅或其他中斷事件而受到負面影響。
本公司可能需進行重大資本支出以跟上產業內之技術發展。
本公司不擁有對業務至關重要之某些智慧財產權及工具。
本公司可能涉及智慧財產權訴訟，此可能對本公司獲利產生重大且不利之影響。
本公司營運依賴於廠房，而廠房可能面臨物理及其他風險，此等風險可能幹擾生產。
本公司業務若失去某些關鍵員工之服務，可能會受到影響。
若我方 subcontractors 或 suppliers 未能履行其契約義務，我方契約獲利能力及獲取新契約之能力可能會受到不利影響。
未來疫情及傳染病爆發可能對本公司業務、營運成果、財務狀況及流動性造成重大不利影響。
戰略與財務風險
本公司依賴持續取得融資以經營業務及執行業務策略，且可能無法在本公司可接受之條件下取得額外融資。
本公司現有債務包含限制性及財務契約條款。
我方稅務提列之未預期變動或對額外所得稅負擔之曝露，可能會影響我方獲利能力。
本公司營運成果可能因商譽或其他無形資產減損而受到不利影響。
本公司對變動利率及外幣交換率之曝露，可能對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況造成重大且不利之影響。
法律及法規風險
本公司受重大政府法規管制，可能需支出重大費用以符合新或更嚴格之政府法規。
本公司受美國反貪污法（FCPA）及其他反貪污法規、出口管制法規、進口及關稅法規、貿易及經濟制裁法規及其他規範本公司營運之法規所規範。
本公司業務及財務成果可能受各種訴訟及法規程序之影響。
本公司飛機零組件之上設押可能高於該飛機零組件之價值，可能對本公司收回、租賃或出售該飛機零組件之能力造成負面影響。
在某些國家，安裝於飛機上之引擎可能成為飛機之組成部分，本公司可能無法行使對該引擎之所有權權利。
本公司產業易受產品及其他責任索賠之影響，且未充分投保之索賠可能對本公司營運成果及財務狀況造成不利影響。

paragraphs: 您應仔細審閱下列所描述的風險與不確定性，以及本年度報告中的其他資訊，再做是否投資本公司普通股的決定。若任何上述風險發生，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果或前景造成重大且不利的影響，進而導致本公司普通股的市場價格下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。本年度報告中亦包含涉及風險與不確定性的展望性陳述。請參閱本年度報告中「關於展望性陳述的特別說明」。本公司實際結果可能與這些展望性陳述中預期的有重大且不利的差異，原因包括下列所列等因素。
我們從世界各地的供應商處取得用於業務的零件與零組件。目前的國際政治形勢，包括制裁及其他貿易限制措施與國家間關係，可能導致重大材料與零件短缺，以及交貨延誤、人力短缺、物流問題、能源成本上升與價格上漲。這些問題可能導致重大供應商表現失敗與延誤。若我們的供應鏈與業務運作，或我們供應商的供應鏈與業務運作受到幹擾，將可能對我們提供後市場支援與服務給客戶的能力造成不利影響。

作為商業航空產業的產品與服務供應商，我們通常會受到該產業總體經濟狀況的影響。商業航空產業歷來具有週期性，過去曾因國際政治事件，例如政治不穩定（包括俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間、以色列與哈瑪斯之間，以及最近因美國與以色列在伊朗的軍事行動），升級的緊張關係（例如中國與美國之間），恐怖主義，高燃油與石油價格，勞動問題，缺乏資金，持續通貨膨脹，高利率與弱勢經濟狀況而受到負面影響。由於這些及其他事件，我們的部分客戶曾申請破產保護或停止營運。全球金融市場的不穩定影響，已導致並可能在未來導致航空公司減少國內或國際運力。此外，我們的部分航空公司客戶過去曾因緊縮的信貸市場而受到影響，這限制了他們購買零件、服務與飛機設備的能力。

美國與國外的飛機飛行活動減少，已導致並可能持續導致受影響飛機類型的零件支援與維護活動需求減少。此外，緊縮的信貸條件會降低購買零件、服務與飛機設備的流動性。航空業環境惡化也可能導致更多航空公司破產，在此情況下，我們可能無法完全收回應收帳款。因弱勢經濟狀況導致的客戶需求減少，包括緊縮的信貸條件與客戶破產，可能對我們的財務狀況或營運結果造成不利影響。全球經濟減速，或經濟衰退，將對商業航空產業造成負面影響，並可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、流動性與營運結果產生重大不利影響。
我們能否透過有利條件取得使用中的飛機設備，以作為銷售USM零件的原料，是我們能否在飛機設備壽命週期結束前獲利管理飛機設備的重要因素之一。我們若無法取得飛機設備，可能對我們的財務狀況或營運結果造成不利影響。我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與成長率可能
